sources.title: Building foundational models using Weight Space Programming
sources.author: Quillan-Ronin Research Team
sources.access: Read Zenodo API metadata and the full Markdown manuscript; checked listed MD5
notes: Describes analytical direction removal, donor-matrix resizing/SVD, and additive adapter folding.
Cropping or periodically tiling matrices changes dimensions but does not establish semantic alignment across architectures.
The folding theorem assumes constant uniform routing and shared inputs; it does not establish equivalence for input-dependent routing.
The reported throughput comparison changes backend and precision, so it does not isolate an effect of weight editing.

The manuscript does not provide a controlled broad capability comparison sufficient to verify its general no-degradation claim. Linked implementation and model artifacts were not independently audited or executed.
sources.future_use: Consider paired-activation alignment before donor transfer; require same-evaluation quality and backend-controlled throughput comparisons.

sources.author: Boris Knyazev
sources.access: Read original public X syndication JSON, viewed animation poster and quoted keynote slide; full animation not analyzed
notes: Proposes manipulating a learned latent representation of model weights instead of editing individual parameters.
The attached poster illustrates a 207-weight MLP; it is not evidence of successful transfer between our two Qwen models.
The quoted keynote slide distinguishes encoder, decoder, autoencoder, and equivariant or graph-based approaches to weight-space learning.
sources.future_use: A learned weight encoder/decoder could provide a compact edit space, but compatibility, parameter symmetries, training data and preservation of model behavior would need validation.
